title: Unified attempt record (Phase 1 P1-2, v2)
description: One strict Draft 2020-12 record: the canonical v2 attempt envelope per D209 as mapped by docs/staffing/phase1-contracts.md, unifying the lee-llm-router run-command attempt, the Agent-Orch model/effort observation (/home/lee/projects/auto-orch/src/auto_orch/performance.py OBSERVATION_SCHEMA), and the AI Workforce Benchmark crew-run record (/home/lee/projects/ai-workforce-benchmark/config/crew-run.schema.json). The v1 source-specific payloads remain embedded verbatim as provenance evidence; they are not competing locations for v2 usage, cost, selection, or verdict. Route identity is exactly the tuple (model, effort, harness, channel) per the accepted P0-1 route contract (phase0-contracts §Route); provider is separate optional observed metadata, never part of the identity tuple, never a replacement for channel, and never invented for a source that lacks one. class_record reproduces the strict classes.schema.json $defs/classBlock vocabulary verbatim (same six required fields, same closed value sets, same canonical class_key pattern); imported historical attempts without class metadata omit it and carry class_source: 'none' — the only condition under which class_key is optional. Per D206, quoted verbatim: 'Class metadata MUST NOT map directly to a preferred model or route. It may only: 1. join production attempts to comparable benchmark evidence; and 2. determine whether an unevidenced cheap trial is permitted.' No class-to-model or class-to-route mapping exists in this schema. verified_success is true only for verdict 'pass' with the required route, usage, cost (when usage permits it), oracle, duration, and provenance evidence; where a source lacks a channel, provider, supervisor route, usage, cost, or duration, the field is null or absent — never invented. Every price, fee, capacity, date, or multiplier needs a source; this schema invents none. Phase 1 P1-7b1 (Chief of Staff answer 3, docs/staffing/chief-answers-p1-3.md) adds record_kind 'agent_orch_attempt': the agent-orch runs per-attempt import built only from the authorized raw per-attempt artifacts ($defs/agentOrchAttempt), with class_source 'none' and never class_record, provenance.source 'agent-orch-runs', the verdict tier 'engine_validation', and verified_success exactly the agent-orch validation gate (worker_exit_code == 0 and validation_passed == true). The existing 'agent_orch' full-observation kind is unchanged and reserved for the Phase 4 import. The benchmark_run payload has exactly two shapes selected by oneOf ($defs/benchmarkRunPayload): $defs/crewRunRecord, the historical crew-run envelope retained so append-only ledger lines committed before the raw-v6 repair stay valid and readable — it is no longer written by any importer, because the benchmark v6 staffing-evidence sidecar provides neither a crew name nor a crews-file identity; and $defs/benchmarkV6Run, the raw v6 shape whose payload contains only facts read from the verified sidecar and its SHA-256-pinned source CSV, so no crew or crews-file semantics are ever invented. Because the ledger is append-only, pre-repair legacy rows are never rewritten: re-running the benchmark import appends a deterministic benchmark:v6:<run_id> correction record for each legacy-shaped row whose run is present in the verified source, leaving the fabricated legacy line in place as disclosed history.

schema_version.description: v2 attempt envelope (phase1-contracts §Attempt record v2 placement).

attempt_id.description: Caller-supplied attempt identifier. Pattern taken verbatim from the benchmark crew-run attempt_id; a real Agent-Orch attempt id (e.g. a6a85c6b02c6) matches it. Imports are idempotent by this deterministic id.

record_kind.description: Which source produced the attempt; the matching source payload is required (see allOf). 'agent_orch' and 'benchmark_run' are imports embedding their v1 payloads verbatim; 'router_run' is a live run-command attempt whose provenance payload is the router ledger dispatch event. 'agent_orch_attempt' (P1-7b1, Chief answer 3) is the agent-orch runs per-attempt import built only from the authorized raw per-attempt artifacts; it never carries the full observation payload, which remains the Phase 4 'agent_orch' shape. v2 drops the v1 'interactive' kind: a bare dispatch event records no outcome and is not an attempt; dispatch events remain in the events ledger under events.py's own shape, and the router_event payload survives as provenance evidence on router_run records.

captured_at.description: When the record was captured, aware UTC date-time (analogous to events.py ts and crew-run provenance.assembled_at).

verified_success.description: True only for verdict 'pass' with the required route, usage, cost (when usage permits it), oracle, duration, and provenance evidence genuinely present (enforced by the allOf gate below): usage must be authoritative and non-unavailable with a source and the input/output token fields the current P0-4 pricing needs, while genuinely unknown optional cached_input_tokens/reasoning_tokens stay null (authoritative harness output may omit those optional components). total_tokens stays truthful: optional/null unless authoritatively reported or calculated. Cost may carry basis ['list', 'marginal'] with both figures, or the sole member ['unavailable'] (Phase 3 P3-7 answer 2): a subscription channel's per-token cost is a list-equivalent estimate, never metered spend, and many subscription-only route models have no committed dated price at all, so its absence never withholds verification on its own; the run command, not this schema, gates that exception to a channels.yaml 'subscription' channel. A source that reports success without complete evidence yields false — missing evidence is never invented to reach true. For record_kind 'agent_orch_attempt' (P1-7b1) verified_success instead means exactly the agent-orch validation gate — worker_exit_code == 0 and validation_passed == true, enforced as a schema equivalence — and the full oracle-evidence gate above is bypassed for that kind only; all other kinds keep the gate unchanged.

verified_success_reason.description: Exact machine reason verified_success is false (P1-4 ruling 3, docs/staffing/chief-answers-p1-4.md). The run command records it on every false router_run record it builds; a verified_success true record never carries one (forbidden by the first allOf gate below). Conditional presence keeps the committed ledger lines and every shipped import example valid: imports without the field stay valid. The vocabulary is closed, and a false router_run record with a non-null supervisor_route (attested) is required to carry a truthful non-unattested reason (last allOf gate below): supervisor_route_unattested (no attested supervisor route was supplied), worker_dispatch_failed (worker exit nonzero or ceiling timeout), oracle_not_passed (oracle verdict not pass: unverified, nonzero exit, launch failure, or ceiling timeout), evidence_incomplete (a remaining route/usage/cost/duration evidence gate does not hold).

packet_id.description: Top-level packet fact (D209): the packet driving this attempt. Required for router_run records; imports predate packets and omit it.

parent_attempt_id.description: Link fact (D209): parent attempt of an escalation. Nullable/optional for an initial attempt; an escalation requires both this and escalation_reason (allOf below).

escalation_reason.description: Link fact (D209): why this attempt escalates from parent_attempt_id. Nullable/optional for an initial attempt; an escalation requires both.

oracle_cmd.description: Oracle fact (D209): the oracle command whose exit status produced the verdict (exit 0 = pass, nonzero = fail, no oracle = unverified). Null/absent for unverified attempts and for imports without an oracle command.

verdict.description: Legacy record kinds use the canonical v2 oracle verdict string pass | fail | unverified. An agent_orch_attempt instead carries the closed object {tier: engine_validation}: that tier means agent-orch's own exit-code plus validation gate, never a deterministic/judge/human oracle chosen by this repository. The record-kind conditionals keep the two shapes disjoint; engine_validation is deliberately not a member of the canonical verdict string enum.

failure_class.description: Failure taxonomy. Exactly five values are proven by the P0-9a task contract (platform_timeout, platform_env, spec_rejected, capability_rejected, unaccounted_spend); no named source proves others, so none are added. Null means no failure recorded (required to be null when verified_success is true).

supervisor_route.description: Supervisor route of the attempt, present only when the source records one (named-crew contract: a named crew carries a supervisor route). Null or absent when the source records no supervisor route; never invented. Null is the explicit 'the source records no supervisor route' marker.

class_source.description: Marks the absence of class metadata: the only permitted value is 'none', and it is required on imported historical attempts (record_kind agent_orch or benchmark_run) that omit class_record. It is the only condition under which class_key is optional. Forbidden together with class_record (allOf below); router_run attempts always carry class_record.

cost.description: Legacy record kinds use $defs/cost. agent_orch_attempt uses the narrower $defs/agentOrchAttemptCost so a measured raw usage.json cost can be identified as list basis without inventing a marginal figure.

wall_clock_ms.description: Observed wall-clock duration in milliseconds, or null when the source does not record one (Agent-Orch observations carry none; benchmark stages/totals carry elapsed_ms). Never estimated or invented.

basis.description: Authoritative non-unavailable usage only; the gate never accepts 'unavailable'.

input_tokens.description: Required by the gate: current P0-4 pricing needs known input tokens (list input/output/cache rates).

output_tokens.description: Required by the gate: current P0-4 pricing needs known output tokens (list input/output/cache rates).

cost.description: Priced cost (basis ['list', 'marginal']) is required whenever the selected channel is metered spend evidence. A subscription channel's cost is a list-equivalent estimate, never metered spend (usage-truth rule): many subscription-only route models carry no committed dated price at all, so basis ['unavailable'] is also accepted here — the run command (loader work, not this schema) gates that exception to channels whose committed channels.yaml kind is exactly 'subscription', never to a metered or unrecognised channel.

allOf.description: P1-4 ruling 3: a verified_success true record never carries a verified_success_reason — a success has no reason field.

P1-4 ruling 3: an attested (non-null supervisor_route) false router_run record must carry a truthful non-success reason, and that reason is never supervisor_route_unattested — the route was attested. Legacy and import kinds are untouched: records without the field (including every committed ledger line and shipped example) remain valid.

canonicalVerdict.description: Canonical v2 oracle verdict for the three pre-existing record kinds. This enum is unchanged by P1-7b1; engine_validation is a tier in agentOrchAttemptVerdict, not a verdict string.

agentOrchAttemptVerdict.description: Verdict provenance for a raw agent-orch attempt. engine_validation means the result is exactly agent-orch's own worker-exit and validation gate; it is not an oracle selected by lee-llm-router.

agentOrchAttemptCost.description: Cost mapping for agent_orch_attempt only. A measured usage.json supplies one verbatim list-basis figure; unavailable accounting supplies no figure. No marginal cost is inferred.

agentOrchAttempt.description: Authorized raw per-attempt facts only, copied from run.json plus the attempt's route-selection.json and usage.json when present. It deliberately excludes the synthesized Phase 4 agentOrchObservation fields and all class metadata.

accounting_status.description: Verbatim usage.json accounting_status, or null when the attempt has no usage.json receipt.

usage.description: Token fields copied from usage.json when present. Names retain the raw agent-orch receipt vocabulary.

source_paths.description: Exact paths of the raw files read for this attempt; a missing usage.json is omitted rather than invented.

provenance.description: Record-level provenance: which system produced this attempt record and which named sources it cites. v2 adds the required discriminant 'source': 'benchmark' and 'agent-orch' mark imports; 'router-run' marks a live run-command attempt. It pairs with record_kind (benchmark_run<->benchmark, agent_orch<->agent-orch, router_run<->router-run) and is enforced by the top-level allOf. The v1 source-specific payloads (router_event, agent_orch_observation, benchmark_run) remain provenance evidence inside this object's record, never competing locations for v2 usage, cost, selection, or verdict.

source.description: Producing system: 'benchmark' or 'agent-orch' for imports, 'router-run' for live run-command attempts (phase1-contracts §Attempt record v2 placement).

source_refs.description: References to the named sources that justify this record's fields.

worker_output_dir.description: Optional absolute path to the directory persisting worker stdout and stderr per attempt, or null when persistence failed.

route.description: Route identity is exactly the tuple (model, effort, harness, channel), per the accepted P0-1 route contract (phase0-contracts §Route; routes.schema.json $defs/route). 'provider' is separate optional observed metadata: it is not part of the identity tuple, is never a replacement for channel, and is null/absent when the source does not observe a provider — never invented. Observed attempt evidence only; never derived from class metadata (D206).

model.description: Model identifier; part of the route identity tuple.

effort.description: Model effort dial; part of the route identity tuple. Null only where the harness has no effort dial.

harness.description: Harness identifier; part of the route identity tuple.

channel.description: Channel identifier; part of the route identity tuple. Must match a channel_id in the channel catalog (cross-catalog check is loader work).

provider.description: Optional observed provider metadata. Not part of the route identity tuple, never a replacement for channel, and null/absent when the source does not observe a provider.

channel_instance.description: Optional observed channel-instance metadata. Not part of the route identity tuple, and null/absent when the source records no instance.

classRecord.description: The strict classes.schema.json $defs/classBlock vocabulary, reproduced verbatim: same six required fields (class_key plus the five components), same closed value sets, same canonical class_key pattern. Per D206, quoted verbatim: 'Class metadata MUST NOT map directly to a preferred model or route. It may only: 1. join production attempts to comparable benchmark evidence; and 2. determine whether an unevidenced cheap trial is permitted.' No class-to-model or class-to-route property exists here and none may be added; the five components are authoritative for validation and class_key is the canonical string rendering (role/oracle_type/domain_tags/size_band/language with tags sorted ascending by codepoint, deduplicated, '+'-joined, and the empty set rendered as the literal 'none', never an empty segment). Cross-field equality between class_key and the components, plus sortedness/dedup of the key segment beyond what the pattern enforces, is loader work (catalog.validate_class_block); the attempt ledger additionally enforces that equality (canonical reconstruction of the five components) on every appended and read attempt record so evidence joins stay reliable — no class-to-model lookup.

class_key.description: Canonical key string: role/oracle_type/domain_tags/size_band/language, with the domain-tags segment the literal 'none' for the empty tag set, or one or more tags from the closed set joined by '+' (sortedness and dedup of the segment are loader-enforced). An empty segment (doubled slash) is rejected.

role.description: Class role; member of the closed role value set.

oracle_type.description: Oracle kind for this class; member of the closed oracle_type value set.

domain_tags.description: Domain tags; the closed seven-tag vocabulary, unique members, possibly empty. This is the authoritative component for the third key segment.

size_band.description: Size band; member of the closed size_band value set.

language.description: Primary language; member of the closed language value set.

usage.description: Token usage for the attempt (D209 v2 placement). 'basis' is the narrowest truthful basis: observed | provider_reported | calculated | unavailable. A non-unavailable basis requires 'source': for 'provider_reported' it is exactly one of the phase1-contracts §Usage evidence taxonomy harness strings, while 'observed' and 'calculated' use a nonempty authoritative source description (never one of those provider_reported strings); 'unavailable' requires 'unavailable_reason' and forbids 'source' and every token counter — unavailable means the tokens are unavailable, never hidden numeric evidence. Token counters are nonnegative integers when reported and null or absent when unknown; total_tokens stays null/absent unless the source authoritatively reports it or it is calculated from authoritatively reported components. Zero is evidence only when the source actually reports zero; it is never an unknown sentinel, and no parser estimates tokens from text, context length, cost, or elapsed time.

source.description: Required iff basis is not 'unavailable'. For 'provider_reported': exactly one of the authoritative phase1-contracts §Usage evidence taxonomy strings (closed enum, enforced below), including the P1-7b1 raw-attempt source agent-orch usage.json. For 'observed' or 'calculated': a nonempty authoritative description of the observing or calculating source — never one of the provider_reported harness strings (enforced below). Forbidden when basis is 'unavailable'.

unavailable_reason.description: Specific missing-event/output reason, required iff basis is 'unavailable' (e.g. 'text mode' for supervisor Pi attempts until P1-4a).

source.description: provider_reported pairs only with the exact phase1-contracts §Usage evidence taxonomy harness evidence strings — never a free-text description.
enum: opencode worker-written usage.json from provider output

source.description: observed/calculated cite a nonempty authoritative source description of the observer or calculation — never falsely paired with a provider_reported harness evidence string.

enum: opencode worker-written usage.json from provider output

tokenCounter.description: Nonnegative integer token count when reported; null or absent when unknown. Zero is genuine source-reported evidence only, never an unknown sentinel; counters are never estimated or fabricated.

cost.description: Cost with its basis (D209 v2 placement; phase1-contracts §Cost rule). Known cost carries basis ['list', 'marginal'] and both figures; unavailable cost is the sole member ['unavailable'] and carries neither figure. Figures are JSON numbers derived from known tokens and the selected dated P0-4 terms; unknown usage produces ['unavailable'] and no numeric cost (enforced by the top-level usage-cost allOf). Harness cost estimates and subscription fees are provenance notes, never attempt-token cost substitutes. The governing dated-terms citation lives in provenance (source_refs/notes) or the pricing snapshot fields, never in an invented number. The pricing_snapshot_ref and pricing_snapshot_sha256 fields are pre-existing, accepted Phase 0 baseline fields (P0-9a, accepted by D208): they are carried forward unchanged into v2 — not D209 additions — and they cite the dated-terms pricing snapshot only, never a competing usage or cost fact.

basis.description: Exactly ['list', 'marginal'] when the dated P0-4 terms price the known tokens (both figures stored), or the sole member ['unavailable'] otherwise.

usd_list.description: List-cost JSON number from list input/output/cache rates; present only with known cost.

usd_marginal.description: Marginal-cost JSON number (same token quantities after the channel badge multiplier selected at the attempt timestamp); present only with known cost.

pricing_snapshot_ref.description: Optional dated-terms pricing snapshot citation (null/absent when none is cited). Pre-existing accepted Phase 0 baseline field (P0-9a, accepted by D208), carried forward unchanged — not a D209 addition, and never a competing usage or cost fact.

pricing_snapshot_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the cited dated-terms pricing snapshot (null/absent when none is cited). Pre-existing accepted Phase 0 baseline field (P0-9a, accepted by D208), carried forward unchanged — not a D209 addition, and never a competing usage or cost fact.

eventRecord.description: One lee-llm-router ledger event, exactly the keys in src/lee_llm_router/events.py EVENT_FIELDS, in the shape build_event returns: all seventeen keys are present, with OPTIONAL_FIELDS (ts, host, harness, effort, authorized_by, snapshot_observed_at) filled by the builder and therefore required here, nullable where the builder allows None.

mode.description: The resolution modes events.py documents: strict, flex, or bind.

headroom.description: Funding-headroom judgement wire values from src/lee_llm_router/availability.py Health.

authorized_by.description: Only allowed when mode is 'bind' (events.BIND_MODE); build_event raises otherwise. Enforced by the allOf below.

agentOrchObservation.description: Agent-Orch model/effort performance observation, embedded from /home/lee/projects/auto-orch/src/auto_orch/performance.py OBSERVATION_SCHEMA with internal $refs re-scoped to $defs/aoProvenance, $defs/aoParticipant, and $defs/aoSeverityCounts. Shapes are otherwise verbatim.

benchmarkRunPayload.description: The two benchmark_run payload shapes; exactly one validates (oneOf). crewRunRecord is the legacy Phase-0 crew-run envelope: it remains schema-valid solely so append-only ledger lines committed before the raw-v6 repair stay valid and readable, and no importer writes it any more — the benchmark v6 staffing-evidence sidecar provides neither a crew name nor a crews-file identity, so a crew_run envelope synthesized for a v6 import was fabricated evidence (D209), which is why benchmarkV6Run exists. Current benchmark imports write only benchmarkV6Run.

benchmarkV6Run.description: Raw benchmark v6 staffing-evidence facts for one CSV run, embedded from the verified sidecar/source-CSV join. It contains only facts the v6 sidecar and its SHA-256-pinned source CSV actually carry: there is no crew_name and no crews_file_sha256, because the v6 sidecar provides neither a crew name nor a crews-file identity (D209: preserved source facts, never invented evidence). No stage, role composition, route, channel, supervisor route, pricing snapshot, or canonical cost exists in this shape because the source records none.

schema_version.description: The verified sidecar's own schema_version, copied verbatim.

sidecar_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the verified v6 staffing-evidence sidecar itself. The sidecar is not a crews file and carries no crew identity; this digest asserts the evidence sidecar's bytes only.

source_csv.description: The sidecar's own source_csv block, verbatim (path as written in the sidecar); its sha256 was verified against the CSV bytes before import. The resolved filesystem path lives in the record provenance, not here.

run_id.description: The CSV row's run_id, verified present in the sidecar run_ids.

task_key.description: The sidecar task_key, verified equal to the CSV task_key.

class.description: The sidecar row's validated class block, verbatim; mirrors the top-level class_record (D206: no class-to-model or class-to-route mapping).

worker.description: The four join-verified worker fields (model, harness, effort, model_family) from the sidecar worker block, verified equal to the CSV row. Other sidecar worker labels (provider/vendor) are not carried: they are not needed for the join and would imply route semantics the source does not assert.

usage.description: The raw per-run usage receipt columns, preserved verbatim under their source column names with null for source null/empty. The top-level usage object carries the same counters under canonical names with basis 'provider_reported' and source 'benchmark v6 CSV usage_*_tokens'; this object preserves the source shape.

usage_status.description: The CSV usage_status value (known | partial | null when the source recorded none). It marks omitted optional semantic detail, not estimated counters.

acceptance.description: The CSV row's acceptance value (normalized to the source's own accepted | not_accepted | unverified vocabulary); the top-level verdict maps it canonically.

elapsed_ms.description: The CSV row's elapsed_ms; null when the source records none. Mirrors the top-level wall_clock_ms.

source_timestamps.description: Every timestamp column the CSV row supplies, verbatim; omitted entirely when the row supplies none. captured_at also appears as the top-level captured_at.

crewRunRecord.description: AI Workforce Benchmark crew-run record, embedded verbatim from /home/lee/projects/ai-workforce-benchmark/config/crew-run.schema.json (minus its $schema/$id/title/description envelope). It keeps its own attempt_id; the unified top-level attempt_id mirrors it. LEGACY SHAPE: retained only so append-only ledger lines committed before the raw-v6 repair stay valid and readable; the benchmark v6 staffing-evidence sidecar provides neither a crew name nor a crews-file identity, so no current importer writes this envelope for a v6 import — such records are superseded, not rewritten (re-running the benchmark import appends benchmark:v6:<run_id> correction records).

selection.description: Router selection evidence for a live run-command attempt (D209 v2; phase1-contracts §Attempt record v2 placement and §run command). It preserves the catalog explain evidence — route ids and explain reasons — not a new selection judgment. Per D206 it contains no class metadata and creates no class-to-model or class-to-route mapping; 'explain_cheapest_eligible' records that the run command took the first eligible route in 'catalog explain --json' marginal-price order.

reason.description: Selection reason as recorded by the run command.

explain_ref.description: Reference to the 'catalog explain --json' evidence backing the selection.

excluded.description: All excluded-route summaries: route ids and explain reasons only.
